title: ZIA Bandwidth Control
aliases: why is my bandwidth rule not firing

prose.text: Bandwidth Control decides how much of a location's internet bandwidth each traffic class gets. It is not an allow or block policy: a request is given full or reduced bandwidth, never refused by this module.

steps.label: Does the traffic reach Bandwidth Control at all?
steps.text: It is the last step of the web module, after the firewall and every earlier web policy, and only certain TCP protocols are shaped: [[zia.bandwidth-control.pipeline-position]], [[zia.bandwidth-control.allocation]].

steps.label: Is the location in scope?
steps.text: Only configured locations are shaped, the location must enforce Bandwidth Control and have upload and download limits, and sublocations can share or own a slice: [[zia.bandwidth-control.location-scope]].

steps.label: Which class is the traffic in?
steps.text: Classes group URL categories, cloud applications and domains, plus the large-file, web conferencing and VoIP classes: [[zia.bandwidth-control.classes]].

steps.label: Which rule references that class, and where is it in the order?
steps.text: Criteria, order, admin rank and disabled rules: [[zia.bandwidth-control.rules]]. Provider reorder and rank behavior is in [[zia.terraform.rule-order.registry]].

steps.label: What terms does the traffic get?
steps.text: Minimum and maximum percentages are applied differently, and the minimum only matters under contention: [[zia.bandwidth-control.allocation]]. A class no rule references lands in the default rule: [[zia.bandwidth-control.default-rule]].

steps.label: Is a cap in the way?

prose.text: For API and Terraform work, field names, enums and provider resources are in [[zia.bandwidth-control.api-surface]]. Firewall Control is a different module that allows or blocks flows: see [[zia.firewall]].
